items.headline: Canada seeks industry input on lunar microreactor technologies
items.what_happened: The Canadian Space Agency issued a request for information on lunar microreactor technologies, using a planning envelope of 20 kWe to 80 kWe of continuous net output and at least 10 years of life. It lists 16 areas of interest, from fuel and heat transport to launch integration, and says Canada is not assuming one domestic firm would deliver a full system.
items.why_it_matters: This is lunar power, not a terrestrial 1-20 MW buyer. It names no reactor type, no vendor and no buyer, so it signals interest in Canadian supply chains rather than demand.
items.binding_note: A request for information, not a contract. The release names no award and no selected technology.

sources.label: ANS Nuclear Newswire: Canada assesses its space reactor capabilities (Nov. 9, 2026)
sources.quote: lunar reactor capable of producing 20 kWe

items.headline: DOE approves cost-shared funding for Southern-led 150 kWt molten chloride test reactor
items.what_happened: Southern Company and Core Power announced that the Department of Energy approved cost-shared funding for the Molten Chloride Reactor Experiment (MCRE). It is a 150 kWt fast-spectrum test reactor at Idaho National Laboratory's Zero Power Physics Reactor cell. The approval funds an accelerated final development stage, and criticality could come as early as 2027.
items.why_it_matters: MCRE is a test rig, not a product a buyer can order, so it does not add a 1-20 MW offering. It does show DOE money moving to a fast-spectrum salt design, which matters if a microreactor developer later licenses that fuel and coolant chemistry.
items.binding_note: Announcement of DOE approval for cost-shared funding. The funding agreement text was not retrieved, so no executed award is confirmed here.
